subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class core sleep tool, extend sessions_yield/cron wake into a timed self-pause primitive, or keep the current cron/subagent workaround model?
rationale: The request is valid but creates a new model-facing tool and gateway/session lifecycle contract; automation should not choose that API shape or config policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design core sleep primitive
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved sleep/resume contract in core, with bounded duration, cancellation on inbound user messages, and focused gateway/agent/session tests.

options.title: Extend existing yield/wake
options.body: Reuse sessions_yield plus cron wake internals under a clarified API if maintainers want one continuation mechanism instead of another tool.

options.title: Do not add core surface
options.body: Keep the current cron and subagent guidance, documenting that general timed self-pauses are not a supported core workflow.

recommendation.title: Design core sleep primitive
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved sleep/resume contract in core, with bounded duration, cancellation on inbound user messages, and focused gateway/agent/session tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the broadest recent history across cron, embedded runner, and gateway/session surfaces implicated by the decision.
